canal_p19_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_001.text: The forty-fifth morning began with frost on the boards beside the lock. It melted wherever feet had polished the grain, leaving a surface that looked dry until someone stepped on it. Yue arrived carrying a shovel and the folded ugly drawing. Luo had tied bright cloth to the loose turn during her ordinary round. The mason stood beside six usable pavers selected from the commission's recorded path stock. He tapped each with a small hammer, rejecting one cracked piece before lifting anything into place. The sound carried across the water like an impatient breakfast bell.

canal_p19_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_002.text: Bao came only for his appointed light observation, supported wrist held close to his body. He watched the mason test the bed and correctly predicted where the upper edge would slump. When Yue smiled, he scowled. "Do not congratulate me for sitting." She set the chair where he could see the work without leaning over it. Their old argument about him carrying loads had been easier than this new one about being carried by a schedule. He accepted a cup of hot water from Luo and complained that it tasted of the kettle's private grievances.

canal_p19_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_003.text: The path strip had served walking feet for years. Now the damaged turn needed a firmer edge, not a wider road inviting carts it could not support. Yue lifted surface mud into a basket while the mason opened the sound inner bed by hand. A grain carrier stopped to ask whether his handcart could cross once they finished. Luo pointed to the existing cart route behind the sheds. He groaned at the extra distance. The mason answered without looking up: "If I could make earth strong by making you happy, I would be richer than your mill."

canal_p19_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_004.text: The first rejected paver became an immediate argument. Its outer half looked sound, and the carrier proposed using that part where wheels would not reach. The mason showed the fine crack running underneath. He put it aside for later rubble use only after breaking it to expose the fault. Yue heard the sharp strike and thought of all the small failures that had appeared after someone first said it would probably do. The carrier examined the broken face, then hauled his cart toward the longer route. He returned with two pears, offered as an apology rather than wages.

canal_p19_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_005.text: A woman wearing a white mourning tie came down from the houses and stopped at the temporary barrier. Her mother's funeral boat was due at noon, and the short route led to the old boarding step. Yue knew the step had been little used since the public landing changed. The woman had walked it yesterday and wanted no lecture about improvements. Luo put down her kettle. "We will look at the step before anybody carries a person there." The woman flinched at the phrasing, then said her mother had hated being carried carefully even while alive.

canal_p19_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_006.text: They reached the old step from the sound inner ground. A winter vine hid the lower side, which had looked intact from above. The mason brushed it aside and found a hollow where runoff had taken the fine soil away. He did not test the edge with his weight. Yue marked the place with a strip of cloth and walked back along the safe route. The funeral woman had followed only as far as the agreed standing point. When she saw the hollow, her anger changed direction without becoming smaller. "We told everyone that boat would use the old step."

canal_p19_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_007.text: The boat owner could receive the party at the current public landing, reached by the sound longer path. He had to confirm the time and turning space, rather than appearing merely because Luo preferred the solution. The woman sent her brother with a message through his usual paid arrangement. She remained on the bank, looking at the strip of white cloth on her sleeve. Yue offered to fetch a stool. "I am not the one who died," she snapped. Yue took a breath and stayed nearby without pretending the answer meant she should leave.

canal_p19_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_008.text: The funeral boat replied before the bakery's second tray came out. Its skipper could use the public landing at the same tide, but not the narrow cart corner where the family had planned to wait. The mourning woman went herself to redirect the relatives. Luo kept the old step barrier in place and informed the public path officer through the ordinary office route. Temporary closure did not mean the commission suddenly possessed enough labor to rebuild the entire landing. The mason returned to the small edge repair he had actually been hired to finish.

canal_p19_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_009.text: Yue thought of the woman's abrupt reply while carrying the mud baskets. She had offered a stool as though every hard feeling had a useful object waiting beside it. Bao noticed her silence and asked whether she wanted him to diagnose it from his chair. She told him. "You could apologize once," he said. "Or bring seven stools and establish a reputation." He leaned back before his wrist could help balance him. The kettle steamed between them. Yue was grateful for the joke and still unsure whether the woman wanted to see her again.

canal_p19_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_010.text: By late morning the sound pavers formed a narrow, firm walking edge. The mason bedded them against the existing stable ground and left the new strip closed while it settled. Its width and intended use were marked; it would not carry a loaded cart or substitute for the failed old boarding step. Luo wrote the limitation on a board and then made the young keeper read it from the approach. The girl suggested moving it half an arm's length because a tall barrel hid the last line. They moved the barrel, whose owner objected until he saw the hollow.

canal_p19_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_011.text: At noon the funeral party gathered by the safe landing with flowers, two baskets of food, and arguments about which aunt should stand nearest the rail. No canal worker carried the coffin; the family's hired bearers used their agreed route and the boat crew handled boarding. Yue stood out of their way. The mourning woman passed her and paused. "A stool would have been sensible," she said, almost angrily. "I was tired." Yue fetched one from the landing host with permission. It became a seat for the oldest aunt before the woman could use it herself.

canal_p19_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_012.text: The boat pushed off under ordinary oars. A child dropped a flower onto the water and watched it hurry alongside the hull. The woman's brother began an old farewell song in a voice too high for him; another relative joined and found the missing lower notes. Luo kept her head bowed until the stern passed the bend. Then she checked the return space for the waiting cargo boat. Grief had occupied the landing without making its next duty vanish. Yue helped move the empty stool back inside, feeling less useful and less troubled by that feeling.

canal_p19_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_013.text: The unused boarding step remained a real hazard after the funeral party left. The path officer inspected it that afternoon on his appointed round and extended the visible closure to its sound approaches. He recorded a separate future assessment, with no claim that Yue's small repair budget could pay for it. The old step's owner was not clear in the newer map. Pei requested the surviving public route book before anyone tried to settle that question by who had swept the planks most recently. The inspection closed a danger today and opened a problem for another meeting.

canal_p19_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_014.text: Han came to inspect the changed walking edge because his loaders used the route to reach their houses. He brought a bag of private nails he thought might help. The mason thanked him and explained that this stone edge required none. Han stood awkwardly with the bag, then asked if the young keeper needed to fix her loose stall board. She did, and accepted an exact small quantity as a private gift. Pei later wrote no entry converting the leftover bag into canal stock. Yue enjoyed watching generosity fail to become a reason for another claim on public earth.

canal_p19_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_015.text: The power frame waited in the dry receiving shed, disconnected and covered. Its commissioned stones remained in the marked box with the route-specific readings, not in anyone's personal pack. Luo asked whether Yue could give it one final little pulse while they were there. Yue showed her the receiving plan: dry inspection, witness to seals and fittings, no powered appointment. Jiang's work had ended and the charged store was finite. Luo sighed, then fetched the actual gauge and papers. "I liked the other answer better before you gave it," she admitted.

canal_p19_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_016.text: Bao read the frame's earlier stopping notes from his chair. The last accepted small command had worked within the checked upper pocket condition, not against the force of the storm. The surviving charge floor was two hundred forty-four units, with higher actual balances on some earlier choices. The keeper had to carry the exact selected readings forward. A tidy single estimate could not replace them. Yue copied the relevant figures onto the receiving cover and returned the original sheets to the case. For once, Bao found nothing in her work worth mocking immediately.

canal_p19_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_017.text: The qualified mason's added quarter-day included the remaining physical adjustment of the guide bracket under an unloaded frame. He loosened it with the proper tool while Yue held the ordinary reference rule clear of his hands. Bao could describe the earlier misalignment but did not grip the tool or support the mechanism. The dry adjustment moved nothing under water pressure. Afterward the mason checked the stops and tightened the fitting to the specified mark. Luo watched so closely that the young keeper asked whether she intended to memorize the screws' individual faces.

canal_p19_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_018.text: There were three receiving questions still worth pursuing before the physical return work closed. The changed path needed a real walk after its bed settled. The dry frame case needed a complete handover, including the limit on future use. The private storage corner beside the cart route needed clearing without pretending those goods were public spoil. Yue could spend her next agreed task interval on one of them. Other assigned people would cover the remaining duties and report their actual results. Bao said he would spend his own interval going home and taking the clinician seriously for once.

canal_p19_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_019.text: The storage corner held empty barrels, two folded tarpaulins, and a cart axle belonging to three different owners. After the flood people had put everything on the highest convenient patch and left it there. That patch now narrowed the sound route to a sideways shuffle. Han offered his yard for one owner's barrels, but the owner suspected a storage fee would arrive afterward. Han wrote the exact short arrangement on a scrap and asked the owner to read it. The tarpaulin keeper was away until evening. No one moved her property merely to finish the task sooner.

canal_p19_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_020.text: The new path bed needed the mason's stated settling interval, so Luo delayed the first walk until next morning. The young keeper wanted to test her warning route at the same time. A funeral relative had already tied another mourning ribbon to the old step barrier, which made it more conspicuous without making the closure permanent. Yue checked that the ribbon did not cover the warning. From the landing she could see an ordinary boat choosing the correct approach. The longer route was inconvenient, but today it had carried both mourning and grain without asking either to become weightless.

canal_p19_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_021.text: Tian passed on her way to a customer, wearing a coat whose hem she had repaired with a slightly different color. She asked what had stopped the funeral boat from using the old step. Yue showed her the inspection drawing. Tian studied it, then pointed at the word "future" beside the separate repair assessment. "That means after people have forgotten to be frightened." Yue thought of the white ribbon. "We need the closure to survive that." Tian pulled a length of bright waste cloth from her basket and offered it only if the officer accepted it for the mark.

canal_p19_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_022.text: The officer accepted the visible strip as a voluntary small material contribution and noted its source; it did not make Tian responsible for inspecting the step. She had expected no appointment but still looked relieved to hear it said. Han laughed softly from the cart corner. "Every time anyone gives you something, you wrap a rope around the gift so it cannot grow legs." Tian replied that his earlier notices had taught the town to watch for legs. He took the answer without pretending it was affection. Yue looked away to hide the beginning of a smile.

canal_p19_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_023.text: At supper Bao's sister brought his meal outside so he would stop trying to carry dishes through the crowded room. He complained that she had moved an entire household around one wrist. She said the wrist had already moved his work onto other people and could tolerate one bowl on a bench. Yue had come to return the copied observation notes, not examine him. She left them beside the meal and stayed long enough to hear Bao ask his sister how her own day had gone. The question surprised both women more than another argument would have.

canal_p19_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_024.text: On the forty-sixth morning the path strip looked disappointingly like ordinary paving. The mason checked the bed, edge, and approach before reopening it for feet. He left the old step closure untouched. The young keeper arrived in her market shoes and made her actual receiving walk without jumping over the narrowed turn. At one point she stopped to tie a lace, forcing Luo to wait. "I could do it while walking," she said. "You could fall while walking too," Luo replied. The girl smiled and finished the knot with elaborate, infuriating calm.

canal_p19_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_025.text: The private store corner had not cleared itself overnight. The tarpaulin owner returned before breakfast and found the waiting invitation rather than an emptied place. She agreed to move her cloth to her own shed, provided the ground beneath it stayed dry. Han's yard arrangement accepted the barrels for the written short period without a charge. The axle owner needed two people for the lift and booked them from his own loading crew. Yue saw the path widen without becoming the recipient of anyone's property. The separate agreements took longer than pushing everything downhill would have done.

canal_p19_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_026.text: Pei opened the receiving folder and found one test sheet filed behind the wrong month's toll copy. The reserve applicant had made the error while practicing his route and noticed it on checking. He brought the sheet back himself, apologizing too many times. Pei let him replace it and dated the correction. Then she asked whether he had eaten. The young man had been expecting dismissal, not a bowl of cold rice. Yue remembered her own first careful reports and the mistakes that had survived her care. She helped find a clean spoon rather than giving him a speech.

canal_p19_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_027.text: The repaired guide bracket waited under its cover while the lower channel moved quietly past. Bao's dry description and the mason's actual adjustment could now be compared in the receiving interval. No one had claimed that checking a fitting proved every future wet condition. The boundary between acceptance and a new test would matter when impatient people returned after Yue left. Luo practiced explaining it to Han, who played an implausibly foolish customer. He kept asking whether a larger flood would make the apparatus stronger. By the third question she threatened to charge him for being so extravagantly stupid.

canal_p19_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_028.text: The three remaining tasks gathered their witnesses before the morning grew busy: Luo at the walking turn, the young keeper at the dry receiving case, and Han with the owners of the stored goods. Yue checked the hours still owed under her ordinary appointment. Whichever interval she chose, it would answer a real unresolved question rather than become another demonstration of her qi. The mason washed his tools beside the shed. Bao, already home, had sent a note that said only, "Do not let Luo name the screws. She will expect them to answer."

canal_p19_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_029.text: Yue stood where the path divided toward the lock, the receiving shed, and the private cart corner. From the lock came Luo's impatient call; from the shed came the young keeper counting the case seals; from the corner came a barrel rolling a short distance under its owner's careful hand. The decisions had become smaller than the storm and no less capable of hurting someone if made carelessly. She chose which accepted task to witness first, leaving the others with their named workers and an obligation to report what actually happened.

choices.text: Walk the repaired warning route with Luo Zhen.
Clear the private storage corner by agreement.

canal_p19_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_030.text: Luo began the reopened walking route at the public landing, carrying the warning board instead of her usual lamp. She made Yue walk behind her so the keeper would not mistake a follower's better view for her own. The pavers stayed firm under ordinary feet; the route narrowed at the turn exactly as the drawing showed. Beyond it, the young keeper waited inside the covered doorway. Luo spoke the withdrawal call once. A passing cart swallowed the last word. Yue asked them to repeat the test when the cart had actually moved away.

canal_p19_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_031.text: The young keeper heard the second call and returned the correct reply. The new near position worked under that quieter condition; it could not be called reliable under the cart noise they had just heard. Luo moved closer to the public turn before trying again. That shortened the spoken distance without taking her onto the gardener's plot. Yue marked the changed stopping place. The keeper stared at the old chalk line, which was still visible on a board. "I have spent half this job moving a step at a time," she said. "Water had better appreciate my patience."

canal_p19_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_032.text: At the gardener's door the woman wanted to know whether a warning meant the side channel was already running. Luo explained the difference between preparing to withdraw and confirming a particular path was closed. The woman made her repeat both phrases from outside while she shut the window. Yue listened from the room with the gardener's permission. One word became muffled by a hanging blanket. They moved the blanket, not the garden bed. The woman said she had expected a grander improvement from a commission. Yue replied that the blanket had expected to remain entirely innocent.

canal_p19_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_033.text: They found the grandmother washing her recovered cup beneath the eaves. She could hear the spoken call from the agreed covered place but wanted time to dry the cup before leaving. Luo looked alarmed. The grandmother smiled. "I am joking. Mostly." They practiced the actual withdrawal route at her ordinary walking pace, stopping before the public road where work was taking place. Her daughter waited beside her rather than hurrying ahead. Yue counted no imaginary sprint into the plan. The cup stayed on its peg during the walk, proving at least one joke could end usefully.

canal_p19_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_034.text: A boy had tied a fishing line to the repaired edge. His hook hung in the shallow pocket where someone might reach down after it and step onto the wrong side. Luo summoned him from the landing. He protested that the new stones made a perfect seat. Yue could see he had already caught nothing for a long time. The keeper pointed out the marked walking strip and the remaining unstable outer bed. He agreed to fish from the ordinary permitted bank instead, then demanded that they carry his terrible luck there with the rod.

canal_p19_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_035.text: When the boy's line came free, the hook held a tuft of old rope. He wanted to keep it as a catch. Luo inspected the rope and gave it back after showing that it belonged to no working apparatus. He draped it around his neck triumphantly. Yue thought of how easily such a scrap could become a rumor that the canal's gear had broken again. She asked him to tell the landing what he had actually pulled out. He shouted the news himself, so loudly that three customers turned to look at a worthless wet string.

canal_p19_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_036.text: The outer warning route ended before the old boarding step closure. No worker climbed over the barrier to save a few minutes, though Luo admitted she had once crossed there carrying her supper. The white mourning ribbon had dried around its knot. Yue checked the alternative daylight approach with the young keeper and made the closing mark visible from both directions. The officer's separate assessment would decide that old landing's repair. Their current walk could be accepted while a different place remained closed. Luo accepted this and still glanced toward the shorter route like a hungry person watching another table.

canal_p19_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_037.text: On the return a flour carrier asked to move the temporary board until his cart passed. The board marked the unsafe step approach, not a movable inconvenience belonging to Luo. She showed him the longer cart turn and offered no brief exception. His hired hour was running out, and his frustration was real. Yue helped carry his message to the miller, who could decide whether to pay the extra interval. The miller agreed to the small additional private hire. The carrier completed his route without shifting the danger onto someone who would arrive after him.

canal_p19_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_038.text: At the landing Luo wrote the accepted walking condition and the noisy-call limitation in plain language. The young keeper signed for the route she had actually walked. Yue checked that the cart restriction remained on the same board as the reopening notice. A stranger reading only the pleasant half of the account could otherwise create the next accident. Luo rubbed charcoal from her thumb and asked Yue whether all her future work would be this irritating. Yue said she was still gathering evidence. The keeper laughed and told her to collect some from people who slept more.

canal_p19_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_039.text: The task report reached Pei before noon. Its additions were a shorter spoken distance, a cleared blanket, and a confirmed ordinary-paced withdrawal. No household acquired a standing job from answering a practice call. The closed old step stayed closed. Luo returned to her regular round carrying the board, with less reason to distrust it and no reason to worship it. Yue followed her as far as the lock, then let her go alone. The keeper would be the person remaining here. Today that fact felt like a responsibility shared honestly rather than a debt Yue could never finish paying.

canal_p19_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_040.text: The young keeper opened the dry frame case with Luo witnessing the seal. Yue stood at the opposite end of the bench so all three could see the fittings without leaning into the mechanism. The charged stones remained in their separate marked box. Nothing was connected to a source. The keeper read the label aloud and stumbled over the route notation, then began again rather than guessing. Luo waited with unexpected patience. The girl's market hands were competent with knots and small packages; their speed was useful once she knew which package she was actually opening.

canal_p19_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_041.text: They compared the guide bracket with the mason's dated adjustment note. The reference mark matched, and the stop seated under a gentle unloaded check. Yue did not call this a wet trial. Bao's earlier observation sheet stayed beside the actual worker's account, so describing an alignment did not steal credit for performing it. The young keeper asked why both papers were necessary when the mechanism looked correct. Luo answered, "Because tomorrow someone will swear it was always like this." Yue let the keeper's answer stand. She had learned that fact through enough midnight disputes to deserve saying it herself.

canal_p19_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_042.text: The case contained a worn cord that had served only for tying the cover, not for a load. Its frayed end looked dramatic enough to invite a careless repair story. The young keeper separated it from the rated apparatus attachments and requested a sound cover tie from the already recorded stock. She kept the old scrap for the store's ordinary waste sorting, not as secret evidence of a failed rescue. Yue watched her compare the labels twice. Luo looked pleased, then deliberately found another knot to inspect so the girl would not notice how pleased she was.

canal_p19_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_043.text: The charge sheets held different balances because the earlier work had genuinely differed. They read the original choice balance, the two new stones' eighty units, the two-unit dry inspection draw, the selected storm response, and the later twelve-unit test. The smallest surviving total was two hundred forty-four. Some routes retained more, and their actual meter entries would control future use. The young keeper copied the calculation with the selected lines intact. She did not distribute the total equally across stones when the individual meter readings said otherwise. Yue signed only after comparing each copy with its source.

canal_p19_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_044.text: Luo asked where the power should be sent if another alarm arrived before a qualified operator could be hired. The receiving plan gave no permission to connect it under a different head or let the nearest strong person substitute for Jiang. They read the actual isolation and withdrawal instruction. Ordinary crews would use the safe ground response available under their own appointments; the small apparatus would wait for its rated condition and a funded operator. The young keeper frowned at the wasted opportunity she imagined. Yue remembered how attractive a forbidden extra pulse could feel before its price became visible.

canal_p19_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_045.text: A customer knocked on the shed door asking whether the frame could straighten his cart axle. He had heard it saved houses during the storm and assumed metal work would be trivial. Luo invited him to look at the small mechanism from the safe doorway. He seemed disappointed by its size. Yue explained its accepted movement and load, then directed him to a smith who could inspect the axle. He did not book the smith immediately. An honest referral had not made him richer. It had merely kept a damaged cart out of an unrelated machine.

canal_p19_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_046.text: The keeper practiced closing the case, recording its seal, and handing custody to Luo. Then Luo reversed the roles. During the second handover the girl noticed that the date on the cover had been copied from yesterday's draft. She changed it beside the original and made both witnesses initial the correction. Luo looked at Yue. "I should have tested myself first." The girl answered that she could do so now, if the keeper wished. There was just enough cheek in her voice to make the offer sound like the beginning of a working relationship.

canal_p19_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_047.text: They checked the store door and the ordinary dry shelf that kept the meter notes off the floor. The lock belonged to the commission's store inventory; neither Yue nor Jiang would carry its key into another book of work. Luo retained the named key, with the recorded alternate custodian holding the separate authorized one. The young keeper had access only during her supervised receiving tasks until the trustees accepted anything further. She did not resent the limit when it was written clearly. What she disliked was being told afterward that someone had assumed she ought to know.

canal_p19_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_048.text: At the end the girl asked Yue how it felt when a small command caught. Yue described concentration and the slight resistance she had actually felt, without making the frame sound alive. The girl had hoped for a tale of thunder. Luo said she preferred a machine that did not have opinions. Yue smiled and told them Bao had already warned against naming the screws. The keeper promptly named one after him. When the girl laughed, the shed seemed for a moment like an ordinary workplace instead of the room in which everyone waited for the next disaster.

canal_p19_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_049.text: The signed dry receiving report accepted the corrected bracket, intact stops, separate fuel custody, and readable selected readings. It authorized no new powered work. Any future appointment would need money, an actual operator, and the measured condition, not Yue's reputation left hanging on the wall. Luo carried the case to its shelf herself with the young keeper helping under the specified dry handling arrangement. Yue put away the unused reference rule. There was satisfaction in ending a task without a flash or a pulse. She would not have believed that when she first learned to command anything.

canal_p19_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_050.text: At the private cart corner, Han introduced Yue to the three owners before pointing at their goods. The barrel owner had signed the short free storage arrangement; the tarpaulin keeper had inspected her own dry shed; the axle owner had hired his loading crew. They disagreed about who should move first. Yue asked them to measure the open space rather than compete for it in conversation. The tarpaulin keeper could fold her cloth and leave without any lift, which cleared the first useful patch. She did so while telling the men they had needed a whole meeting to discover hands.

canal_p19_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_051.text: The barrel owner rolled his first cask into Han's yard and immediately tried to leave its bung on the path. Han returned it to him. He explained where the barrels could stand and how long the free arrangement lasted. The owner asked for three more days; Han checked his own next delivery before accepting two. Yue watched both men write the date. The storage was generosity with an edge rather than a trap concealed in an easy answer. When the third cask arrived, it smelled strongly of old plums and made Han regret the kindness for an entirely different reason.

canal_p19_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_052.text: The tarpaulins were dry on top and damp underneath. Their owner wanted to hang them across the walking turn while she moved her boxes. Luo, passing on her round, refused to cover the warning mark. The woman found a place on her own shed rail and tied them there instead. Yue carried only the light folded corners the owner asked her to help with, within her accepted task interval. She left the heavy wet roll for the owner's worker. A simple request had nearly become a way of blocking the route they had spent the morning reopening.

canal_p19_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_053.text: The axle was heavier than the hired loader remembered. Before lifting, the two workers shifted their hand positions and checked the short clear path to the owner's cart. Yue stood back with the written arrangement and did not offer her arms as an extra hoist. Han wanted to bring his private lifting gear around the corner. The workers judged their rated manual method sufficient for the inspected axle and rejected an unnecessary second setup. They lifted together on the agreed count, moved it the short distance, and set it onto the cart without placing it against the public wall.

canal_p19_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_054.text: A washerwoman arrived to claim one of the empty barrels, which she said her husband had lent before the storm. The barrel owner denied this until she described a patch on its inner rim. He removed the bung and found it. Han's storage sheet did not decide their ownership dispute; it recorded whose goods he was receiving under the current claim. They compared the surviving private note at the washerwoman's house. Yue stayed out of that room while they argued. When they returned, one barrel went with her and the others remained under the corrected temporary arrangement.

canal_p19_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_055.text: The washerwoman had expected Yue to order a result. She asked afterward why she had waited outside. Yue said she had no basis to turn two private claims into a command merely because she had helped clear a public route. The woman sniffed, then asked her to carry the barrel's bung while she rolled it. That help Yue could give. At the corner the woman laughed at the plank announcing no cart loads on the repaired strip. "Very well. I shall call this a round laundry basket." Yue pointed to the sound alternate path, smiling despite herself.

canal_p19_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_056.text: When the goods were gone, the cleared ground showed a small patch of settling mud where floodwater had dried unevenly. The mason inspected it before anyone called the cart route fully open. It lay beside the ordinary load line rather than under the repaired walking strip. He marked a narrower safe passage and referred the remaining patch to the path officer's assessment. Han disliked the reduced space because his loaders would have to take turns. He agreed to the mark after seeing the actual soft edge. The public corner would not be improved by privately wishing it wider.

canal_p19_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_057.text: Han's foreman adjusted the loading times on his private work sheet so carts would not crowd the narrow turn. The extra waits belonged to the merchant's business, not to the canal workers' unpaid bodies. One driver threatened to take a faster route across the closed old landing. Han showed him the current written instruction and said he would not pay for such a delivery. The driver grumbled and waited. Yue knew this would lose Han some convenience. She was more persuaded by the lost convenience than by any eloquent promise that he now respected the town.

canal_p19_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_058.text: The owners checked the empty corner before signing its cleared condition. Pei received the current notes, including the changed barrel claim and Han's finite storage dates. Nothing in the clearing gave the commons title to the private axle, cloth, or casks. The warning route remained visible, and the cart passage retained its inspected limit. Yue folded the signed sheet while Han shook plum odor out of his sleeves. He asked whether public work always left a person smelling like someone else's mistake. She said it depended on whether he chose to store barrels afterward.

canal_p19_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_059.text: Yue returned to the lock by the clear public walk. Behind her, the washerwoman's recovered barrel rolled with a pleasant hollow rhythm toward its own shed. Han's yard had become temporarily more crowded, while the route everyone needed was less so. No single heroic act had accomplished the exchange. The work had been a chain of actual requests, inspected lifts, dated arrangements, and people accepting inconvenience before passing it onward. Yue kept the report small enough to carry without grandeur. At the shed Luo asked whether the plum smell had followed her. It had.

canal_p19_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_060.text: The three reports came together late in the afternoon. The walking route had an accepted new stopping point; the frame case had a dry receiving condition; the cart corner had private goods moved and one remaining soft patch marked. Yue compared the papers at Pei's table while the reserve applicant read the headings aloud. A mistake in the order would have made the step closure look like a restriction on the repaired path. They corrected the folder's arrangement before copying it. Outside, the bakery sold its last loaf to a man who had come for gossip and found supper instead.

canal_p19_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_061.text: The mason's path account listed the five sound pavers used and the cracked piece broken for ordinary rubble sorting. The recorded store quantity changed accordingly. Nobody bought new stone twice under different headings. His physical guide adjustment and path finishing fell within the accepted remaining hours, including the quarter-day transferred from Bao. He had completed his ordinary share of one and three quarters equivalents. Bao's four and a quarter included only work he actually performed or the accepted light observations. The clerk marked those totals beside the assignments rather than rounding them up for convenience.

canal_p19_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_062.text: Yue still had closing inspections and report hours left in her own twelve-equivalent appointment. She used the next short interval to check that each actual result matched its receiving condition. The work felt slow because she could no longer earn satisfaction merely by finding a danger. Somebody had to keep the closure visible, the fuel figures legible, and the path restriction understood after the discovery became old news. Pei handed her a cup of weak tea. "You look disappointed that nothing is on fire." Yue denied it so quickly that the clerk raised an eyebrow.

canal_p19_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_063.text: The funeral woman returned on the forty-seventh morning to collect the borrowed stool she had forgotten was not hers. The landing host had already put it back in use. She laughed at herself, then sat on it with permission while waiting for her brother. She told Yue that her mother would have complained bitterly about the changed boarding place and then approved the safer one in private. Yue listened without trying to make this into proof that the morning had been good. A sensible route did not restore the person whose family had walked it.

canal_p19_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_064.text: The woman's brother brought leftover funeral cakes to the landing staff, asking first whether they wanted them. Luo took one and ate it while standing beside the old step notice. She knew the deceased by sight from years of boat journeys and said so, offering no invented intimacy. The brother seemed relieved. He had heard too many strangers claim that they understood his mother. Yue carried a cake to the young keeper, who was finishing her ordinary round. The girl accepted it as food, not as payment for having waited patiently while grief used the quay.

canal_p19_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_065.text: Han's barrels acquired a handwritten departure date large enough to read from the yard entrance. A loader joked that the merchant had learned to put limits even on fruit smells. Han said he intended to do the same for jokes if they became more expensive. The private storage arrangements would end after the agreed interval; owners had current reminders. The released crane and platform remained his listed property, with the future public gear lease beginning only after commission closure. Neither the crowded yard nor the cleared cart corner became a new title document for the canal bed.

canal_p19_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_066.text: The public path officer's separate old-step assessment found that the damaged edge should remain closed through the coming wet period. A larger repair estimate would go to the ordinary road authority with the route book needed to settle jurisdiction. Yue's commission record passed on the inspection without charging its unseen future cost to the ninety-six-copper repair allocation. Luo disliked leaving a broken place behind. The officer pointed to the sound alternative landing and the visible barrier. "Closed is a usable decision when open would be a guess." She nodded, though she did not look comforted.

canal_p19_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_067.text: Tian brought a reply from the sail loft folded inside the customer's own written confirmation. The customer accepted the proposed fitting on the fifty-fifth afternoon, with the loft's observer attending at the named interval. Her winter trial remained conditional on that practical result and her own agreement to the offered terms. Yue checked the hour against her canal closing work. The one personal interval still fitted without moving the orchard proposal or taking hours from another accepted task. Tian smiled, then immediately began worrying about the different cloth in the real sail.

canal_p19_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_068.text: Luo heard the appointment and offered to mind Tian's plant if she later chose the trial. She specified the sunny window in her own room and asked Tian to show her how much water it wanted. Tian stared at this precision, then said the plant preferred to dry a little between drinks. Luo looked offended on behalf of her kettle. "It has tastes unlike mine." They agreed to practice once before the departure. Yue let them argue about soil while she copied the fitting hour into her calendar, grateful for a future problem small enough to fit in a pot.

canal_p19_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_069.text: Bao's sister came to the lock carrying his returned rule. He had cleaned it with his sound hand and left a note complaining that Yue held it as if it were a sword. She said he had spent the evening teaching a younger carpenter to mark a bracket on waste wood without demonstrating the loaded movement himself. The lesson was private, brief, and voluntary; it was not another commission task concealed in recovery. Yue asked whether his wrist hurt afterward. The sister replied that he had admitted only to being tired, which in his case counted as a medical improvement.

canal_p19_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_070.text: At the receiving shed Luo and the young keeper checked that the disconnected frame cover stayed dry through a light shower. No new command was made, so the actual selected charge balance did not change. Eight stones remained commission property in the recorded store. Future work would require a measured head, the correct fittings, available fuel, and an actual funded operator. The keeper could now repeat those conditions without staring at Yue. She put the key away on her own named hook. Yue felt the handover becoming less like a promise to return whenever someone grew afraid.

canal_p19_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_071.text: The remaining ordinary operations money continued to cover the present appointed rounds and office dispatches. The future monthly eighteen-copper gross remained an estimate, divided only when collected under actual conditions. If ice prevented boats or emergency costs consumed the eligible margin, the four-copper debt payment could wait; fourteen payable months did not mean fourteen guaranteed calendar months. Pei underlined the word "payable" for the forthcoming charter hearing. Han read it and asked whether the town meant to wait until he died. Luo answered that she hoped he would prefer keeping the canal open to making the calendar look obedient.

canal_p19_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_072.text: Han did prefer an open canal, though he made the answer reluctantly. His wife had already priced the reduced private winter trade and thought they could keep the smaller loading crew if the gear lease actually began as agreed. Those private estimates stayed beside his own accounts. Yue did not copy the household's whole future into the public hearing folder. What the town needed was the accepted lease condition, the finite debt, and the current service plan. Han needed to decide whether to continue a life that no longer included the grand sale he had once imagined.

canal_p19_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_073.text: The gardener's spring seed order was placed in her own name at the quantity she had chosen. The reed household kept its delivered food grain above the new dry roof line and sorted another stack for sale. The stall holder reopened two mornings a week while replacing the spoiled stock from his remaining private funds. Their earlier losses still belonged in the claims record. The additional ten-copper private hardship support had already gone four, four, and two; no clerk could spend those same coins again to make the new columns look less painful.

canal_p19_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_074.text: Yue wrote to Matron Ren once more through the personal arrangement she had already funded, giving the canal closure date and the requested full review interval. This was confirmation of the proposal, not a report that she had visited. The actual retained orchard arrangement would determine what she owed on arrival; any overdue personal return was still overdue. Pei helped make the dates plain without opening the private patients' details. When Yue folded the letter, she felt less impatient with the distance. The answer depended on people whose days were as occupied as hers.

canal_p19_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_075.text: The forty-seventh evening brought a cold wind that curled the repaired path's new cloth marker around its stake. The young keeper straightened it during her accepted round. Luo had gone home to cook, leaving the girl with the ordinary limited work she knew. Yue watched from the shed and did not follow to improve it. The girl checked the narrow turn, read the closed old-step sign, and continued toward market. A wheel squealed on the longer cart route. The noise was irritating, which meant the cart was at least using the place that could carry it.

canal_p19_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_076.text: The reserve applicant finished sorting the receiving sheets and showed Pei the folder before leaving. He had corrected his own misfiled date and could explain the correction. That was enough for the day's supervised task. Pei turned down his offer to remain unpaid until supper. She had once made the same offer to an older clerk and remembered how quickly it became expected. After he went, she allowed herself to rub her eyes with both hands. Yue put the lamp closer, not brighter, and asked whether the next invitation had reached its intended readers.

canal_p19_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_077.text: It had reached two possible record assistants, one of whom asked whether the short fee included carrying every claimant's papers through rain. Pei wrote the exact expected route in reply and left the decision open. The other candidate wanted to see the office first. A winter plan could not simply be declared staffed because two people had heard it. Yue added their status to the closing list. Beyond the window the canal reflected separate lamps from separate houses. She thought about how often a public account became false at the moment it tried to make all those windows answer together.

canal_p19_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p19_078.text: Luo returned after supper with a slice of fried turnip wrapped in cloth. She said it was for Yue and promptly ate half. They stood beside the lock while ordinary water slipped under the repaired cap. The damaged old step remained beyond the bend, visibly closed, and the restored walking turn led safely around it. "Tomorrow the accounts," Luo said with theatrical misery. Yue accepted the remaining turnip. Tomorrow would also bring the unanswered orchard date, the approaching hearing, and a sail that had not yet been fitted. The town had survived; it still wanted things.
